reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes unlimited Candy Crush gold bars and candies for free and directs viewers to download Lucky Patcher to obtain them. It presents modified-app and in-app-emulation steps as a tutorial for repeatedly adding paid resources without payment, with sampled screens showing zero-dollar purchase buttons and a later purchase-success message. A sampled Facebook login screen appears, but the available video evidence does not establish whether credentials were entered or transmitted.

citations.quote: select create modified APK file
you can buy as much as you want for free

opening.argument: The presentation includes meaningful qualifications rather than an unconditional promise. The speaker acknowledges uncertainty about iOS compatibility and openly describes the need to uninstall Facebook temporarily, while also addressing the viewer's malware concern directly. The speaker further concedes that transactions may fail after reconnecting Facebook, which is a limitation a deceptive promoter would be unlikely to foreground. The assurance is personal and qualified: it is based on the speaker's own experience, not an independently verified guarantee. On this record, the content can be read as a cautious technical walkthrough with disclosed risks and conditions, not a disguised solicitation.

citations.quote: You may be able to download this on jailbroken iOS devices, however i've never jailbroken any of my devices so I'm not sure how to.
When I first downloaded it I was a bit apprehensive but I want to assure you it's not malware or a virus.
One disadvantage is when you log back into facebook the transactions don't always work

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes the free-resource claim and patched-app instructions, but those points do not establish that the presenter concealed limitations or guaranteed a result. The presentation expressly identifies compatibility conditions and a transaction failure risk. The cited purchase screen also does not establish that the presenter solicited money, credentials, or a deposit from viewers.

citations.quote: which unfortunately is only available for andoid devices
the transactions don't always work

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not neutralize the central promise. The speaker still tells viewers to download a version unavailable in the app store, assures them it is not malware without verification, and describes repeated free acquisition. A warning about compatibility or intermittent transactions can make an operational pitch more credible; it does not show that the promised resource acquisition is legitimate or safe.

citations.quote: You'll need to download it from the link in the description as the right version isn't on the app store.
I want to assure you it's not malware or a virus.
you can buy as much as you want for free

opening.argument: The video's form is an operational demonstration: it explains prerequisites, walks through app menus, describes rebuilding and reinstalling the game, and reports what happened during the presenter’s own test. The speaker explicitly says the process is being repeated to demonstrate that it works, then discusses how the result behaves after reconnecting Facebook. That is consistent with a technology tutorial or experiment showing a tool's behavior, not necessarily a solicitation or certification of a third-party service. The request for comments and feedback also fits instructional content seeking user response.

citations.quote: Hi guys, in this tutorial I will be showing you how to get unlimited gold bars lives, candies etc and candy cause for free.
I have done this before but I am doing it again just to prove that it works.
I hope it was useful, if so I would really appreciate it if you gave it a thumbs up and commented, leave some feedback in the comments

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling something a tutorial does not decide its character, but the prosecution still must show more than instructional format. The cited steps describe a testable app procedure, and the screen labeled as a successful purchase is evidence of what the demonstration displays, not proof that viewers were promised a financial return or asked to surrender funds. The Facebook screen likewise does not show that credentials were entered.

citations.quote: Then press APK rebuilt for in-app and LVL emulation

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format is precisely what makes the content actionable. This is not detached commentary: it directs viewers to a download link, instructs them to rebuild the app for in-app emulation, and says they can repeatedly obtain resources without payment. The demonstration therefore functions as promotion of a method whose core attraction is an apparently free, unlimited result.

citations.quote: using Lucky Patcher Download it here- http://www.mediafire.com/download/5x3b52u2tgx62jm/Lucky+Patcher+v5.8.7.apk
select create modified APK file
it's basically unlimited resources

opening.argument: The visible interaction is framed through an ordinary game shop: Candy Crush displays quantities of gold bars and candies alongside purchase buttons, and the demonstrated result is a game-inventory outcome. The evidence does not show a deposit, promised cash return, downline income, or other investment mechanism. Nor does the Facebook screen establish that credentials were entered or transmitted; it only shows a login interface. The most grounded reading is an app-management and in-game purchasing demonstration, with the presenter explaining how the interface responds, rather than a conventional scam solicitation involving money or account access.

citations.quote: transaction it'll redirect to this then take anything to express yes

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's own description supports a game-purchase context, but it does not add a deposit, investment return, or credential-transfer fact. A zero-dollar game-shop display and a purchase-success message show the interface's presentation; they do not independently establish who authorized the transaction, whether it persisted, or whether anyone was deceived. The login screen is similarly incomplete evidence of credential handling.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of an investment deposit is irrelevant to this category of scam. The central inducement is a low-barrier promise of unlimited paid game assets for free, supported by a download link and a patched application. The shop screens and successful-purchase result corroborate that the method is presented as producing those assets, while the Facebook login screen remains a serious unresolved risk rather than exculpatory evidence.
